title: Lesson 33 honorific and pejorative VNC review

groups.title: Honorific VNC foundation and participant gate
groups.proposal: Treat an honorific as a grammatical attitude toward another person or thing, formed from a complete neutral VNC Result. Derive the available causative, applicative, or later preterit-embed path from the typed Source and its participant structure, block self-honorification when the speaker would be the honored participant, and keep English H notation as reading evidence only.
groups.writingJob: Capture a complete owner-issued neutral VNC, preserve its typed Source and participants, select only a structurally and lexically licensed honorific path, add the mainline reflexive relation where required, and enforce the self-honorification restriction against the actually honored participant.
groups.readingJob: Show the honorific attitude, honored participant, neutral Source, selected formation, reflexive relation, self-honorification restriction, and the fact that an English gloss may fail to display the respect encoded by Nahuatl.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses honorific attitude and the honored participant only when the clause leaves a real participant ambiguity. The application derives route availability, reflexive structure, person restrictions, and realization from the typed Source.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the canonical VNC and late-operation owners. Do not add English-gloss, H-symbol, reflexive-pronoun, example-stem, or unavailable-route controls.

groups.title: Intransitive causative honorifics
groups.proposal: For an intransitive Source whose typed honorific analysis licenses a causative formation, run the ordinary causative derivation and make its caused participant reflexive with the subject. Let the Source's morphemic shape and the accepted Lesson 25 machinery derive type-one, type-two, or liā causative shape. Preserve genuinely irregular, suppletive, preferred connective-t, and mood-defective formations as typed lexical facts rather than a productive stem list.
groups.writingJob: Derive the honorific causative from any compatible typed intransitive Source, preserve Source boundaries and causative allomorphy, add the coreferential reflexive object, carry fixed lexical substitutions or licensed alternatives only from typed analysis, and enforce any inherited mood restriction.
groups.readingJob: Show the neutral and honorific Results, literal autonomous-agent construal, causative type and Source-shape evidence, reflexive coreference, irregular or suppletive analysis, connective-t continuation, greeting or welcome use, mood restriction, and non-authorizing examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses among causative alternatives only when typed Source analysis licenses more than one. Causative type, reflexive object, boundary realization, connective structure, and mood consequences are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not create a causative-honorific stem whitelist or expose type-one, type-two, liā, reflexive, connective, spelling, or mood-repair controls. Exact lexeme identity may select only a genuinely irregular or suppletive typed analysis.

groups.title: Intransitive applicative honorifics
groups.proposal: For an intransitive Source whose typed honorific analysis licenses an applicative formation, use the canonical applicative derivation with a subject-coreferential reflexive object and read it as acting in one's own interest. Preserve causative-only, applicative-only, both-available, preferred, and honorific-only facts in typed Source analysis instead of an exact verb list.
groups.writingJob: Derive the applicative-reflexive honorific from any compatible typed intransitive Source, preserve the owner-issued Source and participant identity, enforce an honorific-only applicative where typed, and expose causative versus applicative only when both survive the Source analysis.
groups.readingJob: Show the own-interest construal, applicative shape, reflexive coreference, route availability, preference without coercion, honorific-only restriction, licensed alternatives, and examples as evidence rather than authorization.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses causative versus applicative only when the typed Source licenses both; a documented preference is shown as guidance. A single licensed formation is applied automatically.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not show both formation buttons for every verb and do not create a miqui, chōca, or other example whitelist. Keep honorific-only and preferred-route information as typed lexical analysis.

groups.title: Projective-object applicative honorifics
groups.proposal: Apply the honorific applicative rule to an owner-issued projective-object VNC while preserving every existing object. Add the subject-oriented reflexive beneficiary automatically and preserve the genuine ambiguity over whether subject or object motivates the honorific; a first-person subject rules out honoring that subject and therefore fixes the object reading.
groups.writingJob: Recapture the projective VNC, derive its applicative-reflexive counterpart, preserve object number and roles, and enforce participant compatibility for subject-versus-object honorification.
groups.readingJob: Show the retained projective objects, reflexive beneficiary, literal own-benefit construal, possible honored participants, unresolved ambiguity, first-person consequence, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the honored participant only where both subject and object readings remain possible. The application fixes the object reading when a first-person subject cannot be honored.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not infer the honored participant from English H placement and do not add object-number or reflexive controls.

groups.title: Honorifics from derived causative and applicative Sources
groups.proposal: Allow an owner-issued causative or applicative VNC Result to continue through the same projective honorific rule, preserving the complete derived Source, causer, causee, source, theme, and object topology rather than rebuilding the stem from a formula.
groups.writingJob: Capture a canonical derived VNC Result, add the honorific applicative-reflexive layer, preserve every inherited participant and nonspecific object, and realize the continued Result through the ordinary VNC owner.
groups.readingJob: Show the inner derivation, higher agent, lower agent or source participant, retained theme, reflexive beneficiary, possible honored participant, boundaries, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the honored participant only where the derived participant structure leaves a real ambiguity. Recapture, added applicative structure, object preservation, and realization are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Require an owner-issued derived Source; do not accept a reconstructed stem string, formula, or copied example as continuation authority.

groups.title: Projective-object causative honorifics
groups.proposal: For a projective-object Source whose typed honorific analysis licenses the causative route, derive the causative-reflexive Result while retaining the projective object and preserving agent-versus-patient honorific ambiguity. Treat causative-only, applicative-only, both-available, and alternative-stem facts as typed Source analysis, never an example list.
groups.writingJob: Derive the causative honorific from a compatible projective Source, preserve its object, add subject-coreferential reflexive structure, and apply only typed route and alternative availability.
groups.readingJob: Show causative construal, retained patient, reflexive agent, possible honored participants, route alternatives, stem alternatives, and non-authorizing examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses honored participant and causative versus applicative only where both ambiguities genuinely survive typed Source analysis. A sole route or interpretation is automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not create a caqui, nequi, cuepa, or other route whitelist and do not show alternatives not licensed by the typed Source.

groups.title: Mainline-reflexive preterit-embed honorifics
groups.proposal: When the neutral VNC already has a mainline reflexive object, preserve that object topology and form the honorific automatically as an integrated preterit-embed compound with the fixed lexical matrix tla-(tzin-o-ā). Use the canonical perfective stem for every verb class and keep shuntline-reflexive Sources on the ordinary projective path.
groups.writingJob: Capture the complete mainline-reflexive Result, derive its perfective preterit predicate, incorporate it as the matrix object, preserve its object pronouns, and inflect the resulting tzin-o-ā compound canonically.
groups.readingJob: Show mainline versus shuntline reflexive status, perfective embed, zero preterit morph, fixed matrix, replaced matrix object, preserved Source participants, verb-class realization, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The application selects preterit embed automatically from mainline-reflexive topology. The user does not choose the matrix, perfective class form, object replacement, or bracketing.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not expose preterit embed beside causative and applicative for incompatible Sources, and do not add matrix, perfective, zero-morph, or class controls.

groups.title: Reverential double honorifics
groups.proposal: Build a reverential only by recapturing an owner-issued honorific Result and incorporating its perfective preterit predicate into a second tzin-o-ā matrix. Preserve the original subject-or-object honorific interpretation instead of inventing a fresh participant structure.
groups.writingJob: Require a canonical honorific Source, preserve its participants and honorific analysis, derive the second preterit-embed layer, and realize the reverential Result through the ordinary VNC owner.
groups.readingJob: Show neutral, honorific, and reverential layers, doubled structure, inner honored participant, outer fixed matrix, preserved ambiguity, boundaries, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses reverential intensity and resolves an inherited participant ambiguity only where it remains real. The second honorific layer and its structure are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not permit raw stems, copied honorific spellings, or formula strings to enter the reverential route; require the owner-issued honorific Result.

groups.title: Pejorative preterit-embed VNCs
groups.proposal: Form a pejorative from an intransitive, projective-object, or reflexive Source by incorporating its perfective preterit predicate into the fixed lexical matrix tla-(pol-o-ā). Preserve subject-versus-object disparagement ambiguity where present and allow self-disparagement, unlike self-honorification.
groups.writingJob: Derive the Source perfective, build the pol-o-ā preterit-embed compound, preserve inherited objects and person, allow a first-person disparaged participant, and realize every verb class canonically.
groups.readingJob: Show contempt or scorn, fixed matrix, Source type, incorporated predicate, preserved objects, possible disparaged participants, self-disparagement contrast, verb-class realization, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses pejorative attitude and resolves subject-versus-object disparagement only where the Source leaves both readings open. Matrix, perfective, embedding, and class realization are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add example stems, matrix selection, perfective, zero-morph, self-permission, or verb-class realization controls.

groups.title: Compound-verbstem honorific and pejorative scope
groups.proposal: Apply honorific or pejorative grammar to the typed member selected by compound structure: normally the embed in an intransitive-matrix connective-t compound, the matrix in a lexicalized unified compound, and the matrix in a shared-object compound. Preserve the complete compound Source and transform the member through its canonical owner rather than selecting scope from an example spelling.
groups.writingJob: Recapture an owner-issued compound VNC, derive attitude scope from its typed compound relation and lexicalization, transform the selected member, and preserve connector, shared objects, outer inflection, and all internal boundaries.
groups.readingJob: Show compound kind, embed and matrix, lexicalized or compositional status, selected attitude scope, transformed member, shared-object evidence, participant interpretation, boundaries, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The application derives embed-versus-matrix scope from typed compound structure. A user scope choice appears only if a Source analysis genuinely leaves two grammatical structures unresolved.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not expose a general embed-versus-matrix switch, use whole-stem spellings as scope gates, or rebuild compound members from formulas.
